parts.note: may blossom is the flower of the hawthorn tree
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A film star called May meets an American author somewhere in the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'May' looks like a woman's name or a month, but it is the hawthorn blossom. Nathaniel Hawthorne wrote The Scarlet Letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Nathaniel Hawthorne was a nineteenth-century novelist from Massachusetts.

parts.note: holly is an evergreen shrub
hock is a white German wine from the Rhine

explanation.surface: Someone plants a bush in order to make wine from it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' looks like a verb, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall garden flower with spikes of large blooms, of the mallow family.

clue.text: Bet money earned on Red Leader

parts.note: a wage is money earned for work

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A gambler stakes their pay on the Red team's captain.
explanation.definitionFit: A stake placed on an outcome; a gamble.

indicators.note: outside means the word for saintly sits round the word for home

parts.note: saintly means holy
a bird's home is its nest

explanation.surface: Truly, a saint is someone who lives beyond the household.
explanation.definitionFit: Truly or genuinely, as in 'I truly mean it'.

definitions.meaning: in church, the congregation's spoken replies to the priest leading worship

explanation.definitionFit: A reply, and in a church service the congregation's set reply to the officiating priest.

parts.note: fill in the gap in Orsino's opening line of Shakespeare's Twelfth Night about music

explanation.walkthrough: Twelfth Night opens: 'If music be the food of love, play on; give me ... of it'.
explanation.definitionFit: Orsino asks for a surfeit, an overabundance, of music so that his appetite will sicken.

indicators.note: heard means we want a word that sounds like the surname that goes with Lewis

parts.note: Lewis Carroll was the author of Alice in Wonderland

explanation.surface: A man called Lewis is overheard singing a tune.
explanation.definitionFit: A carol is a festive hymn, a seasonal song sung at Christmas.

clue.text: Sentence attackers with the cat, say ?

indicators.note: say asks for a word spoken the same as the word for a cat's weapons

parts.note: a cat attacks with its claws

explanation.surface: A judge sentences assailants to be flogged with the cat-o'-nine-tails.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the cat' suggests the old naval whip, but it is a real cat and its claws.
explanation.definitionFit: A grammatical unit of subject and verb, a sentence or part of one.

clue.text: The rest erred badly, holding cockfight

indicators.note: holding means the rearranged letters enclose the word for a cockfight
badly means the letters of erred are jumbled

parts.note: a main is an old word for a cockfighting match

explanation.surface: The others made a mess of things while staging an illegal cockfight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges ERRED to RE...DER, which holds MAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: The remainder is what is left over, everything else.

parts.note: a quid is a pound, abbreviated L from the Latin libra

indicators.note: in a down clue, put up means written upwards, so read in reverse

explanation.surface: A Russian gambler stakes nine pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Vladimir Lenin led the Bolshevik revolution in Russia.

clue.text: Member objects to stories being passed on

parts.note: a limb such as a leg is a member of the body
ends are aims or objects, as in 'ends and means'

explanation.surface: A committee member objects to gossip being spread around.
explanation.definitionFit: Legends are traditional tales handed down through the generations.

parts.note: a bloke is a chap, both informal words for a man
a fellow is a man

explanation.surface: One ordinary guy meets another who writes verse.
explanation.definitionFit: George Chapman was an Elizabethan dramatist who translated Homer, the subject of a famous Keats sonnet.

definitions.meaning: a surveyor's chain is a measure of twenty-two of these units, so they make up a chain
spars slung across a mast to carry the sails

explanation.walkthrough: 'Chain-makers' suggests a forge, but the chain is the old length used for measuring land and cricket pitches.
explanation.definitionFit: Twenty-two of these units of length make one surveying chain, and on a sailing ship they are the spars holding the square sails.

clue.text: Fixed idea of new bosses-no one to retire

indicators.note: new tells us the letters of bosses are made into something fresh
to retire is to go back, so the pair of pieces is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Management are fixated on a scheme in which nobody may stop working.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to retire' turns NO + I round to give ION after OBSESS, the rearranged 'bosses'.
explanation.definitionFit: A fixation is a fixed idea that preoccupies the mind constantly.

parts.note: being out of the form or school year is cryptically read as surpassing others, putting them in a lower grade

explanation.definitionFit: To excel over rivals is to be in a different, higher category from them altogether.

parts.note: the ton is an old word for high fashion or high society
bridge is a card game

explanation.surface: A Kent town is a hub for the fashion business.
explanation.walkthrough: 19 is KENT; TONBRIDGE is a town in that county.
explanation.definitionFit: A market town in the county of 19 across, so a centre of population there.

clue.text: Girl finds retreat in mountains unfinished

indicators.note: to retreat is to go backwards, so the shortened range is read in reverse
unfinished means the mountain range loses its last letter

parts.note: the Andes are the mountain range of South America

explanation.surface: A young woman finds a hideaway up in the peaks, not yet completed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreat' looks like a noun (a den), but it is the reversal signal on ANDE, the Andes without their final S.
explanation.definitionFit: Edna is a woman's first name.

clue.text: Relative's friend gets a fair mark

parts.note: an aunt is a relative; the possessive gives the S
an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: Your aunt's companion receives a reasonable grade.
explanation.walkthrough: An AUNT SALLY is a figure thrown at at a British fairground, hence a target for abuse.
explanation.definitionFit: A fairground dummy that people throw things at, so a target at a fair.

clue.text: Fish the main sort of dish in Antony and Cleopatra ?

parts.note: char is a fish of the trout family

indicators.note: sort of tells us the letters are sorted into a new order

explanation.surface: Seafood forms the main course in a production of the Shakespeare play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dish' means an attractive woman: Charmian is Cleopatra's attendant.
explanation.definitionFit: Charmian is one of Cleopatra's lady attendants in Shakespeare's play, and 'dish' is slang for a pretty woman.

clue.text: Dabbles in a form of betting—£24 put on

parts.note: SP is starting price, the odds a bookmaker offers at the off
L is the pound sign's letter, from the Latin libra
24 across is the solution ASHES

explanation.surface: Someone toys with gambling by placing twenty-four pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: Read '£24' as the pound sign followed by 24 across.
explanation.definitionFit: Splashing water about is dabbling or paddling in it.

definitions.meaning: this county is nicknamed the Garden of England for its orchards and hop fields
in Scots, the past participle of ken, to know

explanation.walkthrough: KENT is the county in south-east England called the Garden of England; Scots 'ken' means to know.
explanation.definitionFit: The south-eastern county's orchards earn it the Garden of England nickname, and Scottish dialect uses the word for 'understood'.

clue.text: Companionable old bird on a perch, perhaps

definitions.text: Companionable old bird on a perch, perhaps

parts.words: Companionable old bird on a perch, perhaps
parts.note: an older lady sitting watchfully at the side, keeping company with a young woman at a dance

explanation.walkthrough: An 'old bird' is old slang for a woman, and the picture is of a matron perched by the wall keeping an eye on her charge.
explanation.definitionFit: A married or older woman who accompanied a young unmarried lady in society as her escort and guardian.

parts.note: D is a musical note
the earth is our world

explanation.surface: A memo about global shortages.
explanation.definitionFit: A lack or shortage, as in a dearth of rain.

clue.text: Runner gets the odd rest morning

indicators.note: odd suggests the letters of rest are oddly arranged

explanation.surface: An athlete takes the occasional morning off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner' suggests an athlete, but here it is running water.
explanation.definitionFit: A brook runs, so running water is a stream.

definitions.meaning: a woodworker who makes things from timber
in Lewis Carroll's poem The Walrus and the ... the pair eat the oysters

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is a literary reference to the poem in Through the Looking-Glass.
explanation.definitionFit: A joiner works in wood, and in the Alice poem the walrus's companion devours the young oysters.

parts.note: the cavity holding the lungs, which a fighter fills out; also a box to pack items in

explanation.definitionFit: The thorax houses the lungs, and a trunk or box of that name is filled by people packing.

definitions.meaning: what is left after burning, or a cremated body
read as grate-ful: what a fireplace grate is full of

explanation.definitionFit: Cinders are remains after burning, and a fire grate fills up with them, hence the punning 'grate-ful'.

indicators.note: in signals that the answer sits inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A tug-of-war team is paid the going rate.
explanation.definitionFit: To haul or tug something heavy.

clue.text: Last mount for a Cockney to back

parts.note: the last part of something is its end
a Cockney (London working-class speaker) drops the H, so a horse is an 'orse

explanation.surface: A Londoner's final ride is the one he chooses to bet on.
explanation.definitionFit: To back something is to support or approve it, as when signing it on the reverse.

clue.text: West leaves Lewisham, un happy outcast

indicators.note: unhappy letters are disturbed, so what remains is rearranged
leaves means the letter for West departs from the place name

parts.note: W is the compass abbreviation for west

explanation.surface: Someone moving out of a south London district westward is a miserable exile.
explanation.walkthrough: Lewisham is a district of south-east London. 'leaves' drops W to give LEISHAM, which 'un happy' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Ishmael, son of Abraham, was cast out into the desert, so his name stands for any exile or pariah.

clue.text: Some betoken wisdom in the mouth of youth

definitions.text: Some betoken wisdom in the mouth of youth

parts.words: Some betoken wisdom in the mouth of youth
parts.note: certain molars are called wisdom ones, and a young person's mouth holds a full set

explanation.definitionFit: Wisdom molars arrive in early adulthood, and these biting structures fill a young person's jaws.

clue.text: Monkhouse gets the upper hand-carries on

indicators.note: carries means the word for dominance holds another inside it

parts.note: having the upper hand means having mastery
taken as written

explanation.surface: A comedian named Monkhouse gains the advantage and keeps going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Monkhouse' reads as the surname of comedian Bob Monkhouse, but it is a house of monks.
explanation.definitionFit: An abbey or priory is a dwelling for a religious community of men.
